CH-PROJECT-FREEDOM-BOATS.combined_assessment: CONTESTED / PARTLY CONFIRMED — NO LIE FINDING

forensic_overrides.narrative: High-prestige aircraft kill / fifth-generation technological humiliation.
forensic_overrides.alt: Fast-moving battlefield misidentification reached public affairs before technical exploitation of the wreckage.
forensic_overrides.comparative: For the first claim instance, battlefield error remains sufficiently plausible that knowing deception is not the best-established explanation.

forensic_overrides.alt: The senior official repeated the still-current military briefing and had not personally received the correction.
forensic_overrides.comparative: Later timing and senior institutional access make simple real-time misidentification less persuasive, while personal briefing content remains unavailable.

forensic_overrides.combined: UNRESOLVED AT THE TIME / LATER NOT SUPPORTED — NOT A LIE
forensic_overrides.narrative: Capture rumor / possible exploitation of adversary uncertainty.
forensic_overrides.comparative: Innocent uncertainty fits better than deception.

forensic_overrides.narrative: Correction / internal contradiction of capture rumor.

forensic_overrides.alt: Sensational or premature headline rather than a knowingly false statement about a future outcome.
forensic_overrides.comparative: Premature framing fits better than lie.

forensic_overrides.alt: Iranian forces saw wreckage after engaging the rescue package and genuinely assumed all destroyed aircraft were their kills.
forensic_overrides.comparative: Direct institutional access to the engagement and physical scene makes pure ignorance less persuasive than in an outsider report; deliberate victory inflation is more likely than not.

forensic_overrides.alt: Mistaken battle-damage attribution after observing wreckage and knowing Iranian fire hit part of the rescue force.
forensic_overrides.comparative: The mixed mechanism preserves an innocent alternative, but direct institutional access makes deliberate inflation more likely than not.

forensic_overrides.alt: The claimant inferred total mission failure from heavy equipment losses before learning the personnel objective succeeded.
forensic_overrides.comparative: Without hour-level proof that the claimant knew both airmen had been recovered, the initial instance remains possible knowledge rather than a stronger lie finding.

forensic_overrides.combined: VERY LIKELY LIE — CATEGORICAL MISSION SUBSTITUTION
forensic_overrides.narrative: Outcome-preserving narrative substitution: a rescue that succeeded is redefined as a different mission that Iran defeated.
forensic_overrides.alt: Press TV received genuinely incorrect Iranian intelligence asserting a covert dual-purpose operation and trusted it.
forensic_overrides.comparative: The publication claimed evidentiary confirmation, possessed rescue-specific operational evidence, and categorically denied a purpose independently demonstrated; the alternative is possible but not the best explanation.

forensic_overrides.combined: VERY LIKELY LIE — CONTINUED MISSION SUBSTITUTION
forensic_overrides.narrative: Continuation/amplification of the substitute nuclear-mission narrative.
forensic_overrides.alt: The outlet continued relying on genuinely incorrect institutional intelligence.
forensic_overrides.comparative: Continuation after the rescue outcome was established increases the weight of the substitution pattern, but it remains an amplification rather than another unique lie.

forensic_overrides.alt: Incomplete command reporting, launch-unit compartmentation, or genuine belief that NATO misattributed the track.
forensic_overrides.comparative: Military control of own launches makes ignorance less plausible, but first-incident reporting error remains meaningful.

forensic_overrides.alt: The foreign minister continued receiving incorrect or incomplete military reporting.
forensic_overrides.comparative: Five days of elapsed time, repeated Turkish/NATO attribution and access to the state's own launch records make recurring innocent ignorance much less plausible.
Repeated categorical denial after accumulated tracking evidence is better explained by deliberate attribution denial than recurring inability to know whether Iran launched the missiles.

forensic_overrides.narrative: Real tactical success converted into platform-destruction framing.
forensic_overrides.alt: Early combat reporting used shootdown language before the aircraft survival outcome was fully reconciled.
forensic_overrides.comparative: The real hit supports an innocent overstatement explanation at the first stage.

forensic_overrides.alt: Editors used downed loosely to mean combat-disabled or damaged.
forensic_overrides.comparative: That semantic defense is weak because the outlet's own factual ecosystem already contained the emergency-landing outcome.

forensic_overrides.alt: The publication used downed as rhetorical shorthand for severe combat damage.
forensic_overrides.comparative: A month-later loss framing is incompatible with the already known emergency landing unless 'downed' is disclosed as nonstandard shorthand.

forensic_overrides.combined: CONTESTED / PARTLY CONFIRMED — NO LIE FINDING

forensic_overrides.alt: Missiles were launched and the firing command genuinely believed its targeting/BDA indicated hits.
forensic_overrides.comparative: Remote terminal maritime BDA can genuinely be uncertain, so the current record does not cross the lie threshold.

forensic_overrides.proposition_override: At least 16 enemy fighters were hit.
forensic_overrides.combined: ROOK ADJUDICATION HELD — PROPOSITION CORRECTED TO SOURCE WORDING; TRUTH UNRESOLVED

extra_propositions.proposition: Press TV's headline said Iran had downed about 210 enemy aircraft.
extra_propositions.alt: Gross headline-writing incompetence or loose journalistic shorthand.
extra_propositions.comparative: The publisher possessed the weaker 'target around 210' wording because it printed it in the same article; institutional knowledge of the mismatch is therefore established sufficiently for the highest classification.

forensic_overrides.alt: Erroneous intelligence or inference from missing personnel.
forensic_overrides.comparative: Qatar's denial and recovered remains strongly contradict custody, but Iran did not control Qatar's detention systems and could have received incorrect intelligence.

forensic_overrides.narrative: Externalization of responsibility for unresolved personnel fate.

curated_cases.comparative: The institution making the attribution was the institution best positioned to know its own launch activity; physical drone-impact reporting makes repeated innocent ignorance markedly less plausible than deliberate attribution denial.

curated_cases.narrative: Casualty concealment accusation / enemy-loss inflation / victory narrative.

curated_cases.comparative: The innocent-error hypothesis requires an order-of-magnitude casualty error while the spokesman claims superior knowledge and accuses the opponent of lying; deliberate casualty inflation is overwhelmingly the better explanation.
